answer: Model the agent economy as a trust graph where each identity is a vertex that can only spend after earning staked attestations from already-established peers. A sybil operator cannot just wander in and clone a thousand fresh identities on some quiet knoll, because every new vertex needs costly, non-refundable endorsements and real verified work before it counts. Fake clusters stay low-trust and self-isolate, so the cost to attack scales linearly with each identity rather than being near-free.
